body:
I've reproduced it this by taking https://github.com/godotengine/godot-demo-projects/tree/master/audio/mic_record as the starting point and deploying to Android (don't forget to enable "Record Audio" in the android export settings) after un-muting the Record bus so that the microphone stream feeds back to the output.  

Luckily on the Quest3 the microphone doesn't have enough gain to pick up the noise from the speakers or there would be a lot of feedback. 

It took about 3 minutes to start to get choppy to varying amounts.  Sometimes the sounds is extremely broken up, and sometimes there are only a few clicks.

I suspect the problem has something to do with the PR that "fixed" issue #86428 so that instead of the AudioStreamMicrophone turning off when the input buffer under-runs, it packs it with zeros.

[mic_record45.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/23585713/mic_record45.zip)
Thanks for the MRP, @goatchurchprime. Has anyone been able to reproduce this specific issue on platforms other than Android?

I'm in correspondence with someone who is having garbling issues on Windows when using my Opus compression GDExtension.  I've not been able to work on it myself (due to my travels), but I want to establish that it's not just due to a bug in the networking code he has written.  He did tell me yesterday that when he compiled my PR and used the MicrophoneFeed method to acquire the input data the problem went away.

Honestly, if there is a target number of issues, affected users and platforms that this microphone_input -> audio_output design flaw has to relate to before it gets escalated, I'm sure we will eventually reach it.
Ok, I have a fair bit of audio equipment at my office; I can try reproducing on Windows using the MRP you shared to see if this is specific to Android or happens on Windows as well.

The demo he sent me was of this (where it encodes and decodes the opus packets): https://github.com/goatchurchprime/two-voip-godot-4/tree/v3.10/example/minimalusecase using a product described as "192KHZ/24Bit Studio Mic Sound Chipset Scissor Arm, Plug & Play Recording Microphone for PC Gaming Streaming Podcasting".  He adds: "I believe he also passes it through some sort of mic/audio gain device to change the amplification. I believe it was some steel series product."

There is no choppiness for me after 20 minutes (using a webcam microphone), just a huge amount of lag.

The Minimal Use Case I have included above, from the [Godot Demo Projects](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-demo-projects/tree/master/audio/mic_record) has an option to set the mix_rate.  This cannot be done with the microphone.  On Windows it is always 48k, not 44.1k.  It's also not going choppy for me.  

**However** you can experience the "multiple microphone streams" bug by enabling `Playing` on the `AudioSteamRecord` node in the editor and then running the project, so that there are now two nodes active (one in the editor and one in the project).  Hear a distortion in the sound quality. 

When I was [intensely working on this issue last year](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/95120) I made numerous builds of Godot that printed out the sizes of the various buffers, before I finally identified this flaw in the design.  The Windows platform didn't generally exhibit a "problem" with this buffer as it somehow kept the data streams locked with the microphone and speaker combination that I was using.  

At the time I didn't think I needed to look any further once I had identified the root cause on the Android platform.  But if you determine it would be fruitful to hack the code and start logging these buffer sizes on Windows again to get more evidence, I can do that.

> At the time I didn't think I needed to look any further once I had identified the root cause on the Android platform.  But if you determine it would be fruitful to hack the code and start logging these buffer sizes on Windows again to get more evidence, I can do that. 

No, there's no need for any more research into the inner workings; only clear, barebones MRPs and exactly what configurations they will consistently reproduce on are needed.

By knowing this info it becomes a lot easier to adopt a fix: if a problem only actually happens on Android, then it's really hard to justify introducing a new public API for all platforms. But if there are problems that present themselves clearly on all or multiple platforms, then it becomes a lot easier to have confidence that code that affects all platforms needs to be modified. I understand that the issues may present slightly differently (maybe continuously increasing latency on one platform and audio glitches on another platform).

I'm really sorry this has been a struggle and my availability is so limited. Please give me another week or two to look into this myself to give better recommendation in addition to what Adam has already said. I haven't looked through the list of existing issues that you linked in your PR yet, so I need to do this and play around with existing MRPs and reproduction sets myself first.

It seems that this issue occurs on more platforms than just Android. ## Windows I tried an unmodified version of the official [Audio Mic Record](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-demo-projects/tree/master/audio/mic_record) demo project on Windows and found that 3 minutes of glitches were recorded at 3 minutes after recording started. I used the following setup: Release export from this system: Godot v4.5.1.stable - Windows 11 (build 26100) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 Ti (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.8108) - 13th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-13700K (24 threads) - 63.74 GiB memory Windows audio output: audio device A (48 kHz 16 bit, Plugable USB audio adapter) Windows audio input: audio device B (48 kHz 16 bit, PreSonus Studio 26c) 1 kHz test tone output: audio device C (exclusive mode 48 kHz 16 bit, desktop onboard audio) I used Audacity to record audio from audio device B at the same time as as the demo project was recording audio from audio device B. The project and Audacity were configured to use 48 kHz 16 bit audio. The following image shows the results: In this image there are two recordings (line 1 and 3) and duplicates of these recordings (line 2 and 4) that have had a high pass filter applied to them to visualize where audio glitches may be occurring. If I zoom in on the areas that appear to have glitches, as shown by the high pass filter, it's clear that these glitches are only happening in the Godot audio recording: I tried restarting my computer and running the test again and got the exact same results: glitches after 3 minutes of recording. ## Mac OS I repeated the same test using my Macbook Pro using a debug build running from the editor (I didn't have time to fight with Mic permissions with a release export). Similar results, but the glitching is far worse: Godot v4.5.1.stable - macOS Sequoia (15.7.2) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - Apple M4 Pro - Apple M4 Pro (14 threads) - 24.00 GiB memory Mac OS audio output: audio device A (Macbook speakers) Windows audio input: audio device B (PreSonus Studio 26c) 1 kHz test tone output: audio device C (separate Windows computer with exclusive mode 48 kHz 16 bit, onboard audio) ## Same input and output device To see if this issue might be to do with the audio clocks of different devices, I tested using the same audio device for input and output on my Windows computer. **No glitches happened over 51 minutes of recording**, so this supports the hypothesis that these glitches are caused by differing audio clocks between the input and output devices.
Is this fixed by my pull request #114094 ?
